In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pCD1 is the most complex of the LCR plasmids of Yersinia.

pCD1 has a highly complex structure and that the LCR-related ORF content has been modified by numerous insertions of transposable elements and by the loss and gain of ORFs, including those encoding effector proteins, in a mosaic-like fashion.

pCD1 is a complex and heterogeneous plasmid with a mosaic structure and a history of multiple genetic rearrangements and that its genetic structure and organization is consistent with the hypothesis that it is a composite of two or more plasmids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pCD1 has been sequenced and that its genetic structure has been analyzed in some detail.
the LCR of Y. pestismay be more complex and diverse in structure and content than has been appreciated previously.
the pCD1 sequence and our analysis have provided new insights into the evolution of the LCR and have provided a basis for further investigation of the LCR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LCR-related genes are organized in a manner that differs significantly from that in Y. pesti pCD1 and in the enteropathogenic Yersinia.
pCD1 ofY. pestis KIM is not a single genetic unit, but a composite plasmid that has undergone extensive rearrangement.
